items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And he came down to the club and he sat down and played piano with us

ctx.x: the lead, and Dizzy Gillespie... That's when Dizzy was really schooling Art Blakey. That was the early Bebop period; he was really schooling Art how to play with the band. And Benny Harris, a fine trumpet player, was with the band. Now, he's the one that "Ornithology," the tune that's based on "How High The Moon" changes that became famous through the era. It was a terrific band.

I had met Charlie Parker before then, in Detroit, when he came through there with Jay McShann. I met him down on St. Antoine one night, and we went up to the Studio Club, because Freddie Webster and a bunch of them was playing up there, you know. And previous to that, Ben Webster came through with Duke Ellington, and he had been listening to Charlie Parker lately, and he was very impressed.
